newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks remain higher in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks remain higher in late trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices encountered technical and psychological resistance at mid-morning, losing some early gains after blazing past 9,600 to an electronics-driven seven-year intra-session high, brokers said.
With 60 minutes left, at 0300 GMT, the index was up 81.82 points or 0.86 percent at 9,582.90, but off its intraday high of 9,626.34.

Recently rejuvenating construction shares, which opened higher on a surprisingly high weekend land auction bid by a China Development Corp consortium, turned sharply lower after failing to find fundamental support, brokers said.
Turnover was heavy at T$140.8 billion.
The electronics sector led the gains, jumping 3.37 percent.
Chipmaker Winbond was up T$3.5 to T$68.5, while microchip maker United Micro had risen t$5.5 to T$149.5.
Compact disc maker Ritek Incorp was up the daily seven limit to T$246, rising T$16.

Nationalist Party-backed China Development had surged T$11 to T$178 after winning the right to build a Taipei financial centre at a weekend auction with a T$20.69 billion land-use bid that was double the base price.
